subject: hero-chibi
label: The Card-wright (chibi) — walking avatar

identity.description: Athletic middle-aged Black man, a card-wright artisan, drawn as a big-headed chibi game character. Close-cropped black hair greying at the temples, short trimmed beard, warm dark brown skin, friendly readable face. Wears a slate-grey canvas work apron with brass tool loops over a deep teal rolled-sleeve tunic, dark work trousers, and a hard brass-cornered card case on his hip.
identity.avoid: no sword, no weapons, no shield, no brown leather adventurer gear, no armour, no wizard robe, no cape, no chosen-one insignia

bibleNotes: Same locked person as hero-cardwright (Bible §Rank continuity: sex, age, body type, ancestry never change). Only the art register differs — chibi for the overworld, the detailed hero-cardwright art for dialogue.
Human's identity is CHOICE; the chosen path (card-wright) must stay readable even at chibi scale — the apron and tool loops are the tell.
Bible §Human visualDNA.avoid bans generic adventurers, brown leather and swords. The avoid string enforces it.

palette.note: Deliberately NO colour reference. Passing the courtyard plate as color_image dragged the chibi toward dark stone tones — his face and apron lost contrast and he read muddy against the sunlit paving. Readability of the character the player controls beats palette cohesion.

animationNotes: One v3 pass PER DIRECTION, each pinned via custom_start_frame to that direction's own clean rotation. Pinning is what forces both the facing and the identity — the two things that broke.

pro mode was tried first and failed: it produced grey background artifacts on several frames and rendered BOTH side rows facing the same way (mirror check: same=0.542 vs flipped=0.503). It cost ~186 generations for an unusable result.
template mode was tried before that and produced a rogue frame 43.7 palette units from its own cycle.
v3 + per-direction pinning is the only method that has produced a correct walk in this pipeline.
